objective: Keep a verified festival content supply for every currently open Gling city; incorporate reference analysis into content planning without changing publication permissions.
approved_direction: Owner approved browsing → verified view counts → reference classification/analysis → branded planning, then asked to integrate while keeping festival content continuous.
scope: Bounded extension of the existing four-daily automation through the runbook it already reads. No new scheduler, dependency, server, DB/UI change, reservation or publication in this terminal.
assumptions: Current daily output target remains four distinct event bundles across all open cities, not four per city.
A seven-day target of 28 newly prepared event bundles is an inventory planning floor, not permission to publish or fabricate missing items.
Research runs on a rolling 90-day window and still covers at least 2026-12-31 under prior owner instruction.
Paid Jev calls require separate cost authorization and account configuration.
style: Use existing CITIES and EVENT_TIMEZONES; standard Node modules only; read-only inventory and fail-closed publication/account evidence.
tests: One small real-behavior test for inventory: closed cities, expired/future events, duplicates, preparation vs registration vs per-platform publication, and empty supply must remain distinct.

always: Respect latest fixed brand/template, verified current-year facts, licensing and Gling-first proof.
Keep discovery, prepared inventory, live registration and per-channel publication separate.
Missing evidence is unknown/held, never ready.
requires_separate_authorization: Any paid Jev/other API call or new charging service.
never: Reserve, publish, run a publishing automation or change schedule/account permissions in this terminal.
Overwrite other active marketing work or existing publication receipts.
Use AI scores to bypass fact/license gates.

success_criteria: One command reports cities from the actual open-city configuration, per-city stage counts and refill priorities.
Existing automation runbook contains rolling discovery, minimum inventory and reference-analysis integration instructions.
Offline Jev boundary and real cached reference evidence are discoverable by that runbook.
A current inventory audit is generated without network writes or paid calls.

verified_result.test: One inventory behavior test passed; excludes closed/past/far-future/duplicate/unconfirmed items and distinguishes prepared/registered/scheduled/published.
verified_result.jev_requests: 3 typed request bodies prepared offline, no requests sent.
verified_result.runbook: Existing automation already reads the amended runbook; no scheduling/publishing action was performed here.
